Using the supplied character sheet as the sole character reference, create one head-and-shoulders character reference sheet containing exactly four panels in a strict two-by-two grid.

The overall canvas is square. All four panels must be identical squares with exactly the same width and height. Use two equal-width columns and two equal-height rows, with perfectly aligned boundaries and narrow, uniform light gray gutters. Keep panel sizes fixed and adjust the character’s framing within each panel. No merged cells, unequal panels, inset images, or irregular collage layouts.

Every panel shows exactly one head-and-shoulders portrait of the same character. Strictly preserve the reference character’s facial identity, apparent age, skin tone, eyes, hairstyle, hair color, clothing, and accessories. Retain the reference image’s visual style and material rendering. Use a plain light gray studio background, soft even diffused lighting, and a level eye-height camera throughout. Keep a calm neutral expression in all four views.

Arrange the views in this exact order:

Top left: Frontal head-and-shoulders portrait. The head and shoulders face directly toward the camera, with the eyes looking straight ahead.

Top right: Left three-quarter head-and-shoulders portrait. Turn the head and shoulders together approximately forty-five degrees toward screen right. The nose points toward screen right, primarily exposing the character’s left side of the face, with both eyes visible.

Bottom left: Right three-quarter head-and-shoulders portrait. Turn the head and shoulders together approximately forty-five degrees toward screen left. The nose points toward screen left, primarily exposing the character’s right side of the face, with both eyes visible.

Bottom right: Exact ninety-degree profile head-and-shoulders portrait facing screen left. Show only one eye and a clear side silhouette of the forehead, nose, lips, and chin. The shoulders follow the same side-facing orientation.

Maintain identical portrait scale, headroom, and eye height across all four panels. Show the complete hairstyle, head, neck, and shoulders without clipping the top of the head. Keep each portrait centered within its own panel.

Preserve the correct physical placement of asymmetric facial features, hair details, and accessories as the character turns. Do not create opposite views by simply mirroring the image. Keep the same character identity across all four views.

Output exactly four equally sized square panels in one regular two-by-two grid. No full-body views, extra people, repeated viewpoints, text, numbers, labels, logos, or watermarks.

Using the supplied character sheet as the sole character reference, create one full-body character reference sheet containing exactly four panels in a strict two-by-two grid.

The overall canvas is square. All four panels must be identical squares with exactly the same width and height. Use two equal-width columns and two equal-height rows, with perfectly aligned boundaries and narrow, uniform light gray gutters. Keep panel sizes fixed and adjust the character’s framing within each panel. No merged cells, unequal panels, inset images, or irregular collage layouts.

Every panel shows exactly one full-body view of the same character. Strictly preserve the reference character’s facial identity, apparent age, skin tone, hairstyle, hair color, body proportions, clothing construction, colors, accessories, and shoes. Retain the reference image’s visual style and material rendering. Use a plain light gray studio background, soft even diffused lighting, and a level camera throughout.

The character stands upright in a relaxed neutral stance, with arms resting naturally at the sides and feet comfortably spaced. Keep the same stance across all four panels, rotating the entire character to produce the different views. The head follows the body’s orientation. Keep a calm neutral expression wherever the face is visible.

Arrange the views in this exact order:

Top left: Frontal full-body view. The body and face point directly toward the camera.

Top right: Three-quarter full-body view. Turn the entire body and head together approximately forty-five degrees toward screen right, showing the front and the character’s left side.

Bottom left: Exact ninety-degree full-body profile facing screen left. The face, shoulders, torso, hips, and feet all follow the same side-facing orientation.

Bottom right: Straight rear full-body view. The character stands with the back directly toward the camera. The head faces away from the camera without turning or looking back. Clearly show the rear hairstyle, the back construction of the clothing, and the backs of the shoes.

Maintain identical character scale, head height, and foot baseline across all four panels. Show the entire figure from the top of the hair to the soles of the shoes, with consistent comfortable margins above the head and below the feet. Keep each character centered and entirely inside its own panel.

Preserve the correct physical placement of asymmetric clothing details and accessories as the character turns. Do not create different views by simply mirroring the image. For rear details absent from the reference, naturally extend the existing hairstyle and clothing construction without inventing new decorations or accessories.

Output exactly four equally sized square panels in one regular two-by-two grid. No close-ups, cropped heads, cropped feet, extra people, repeated viewpoints, text, numbers, labels, logos, or watermarks.

Use the input image as the sole reference and create a higher-definition version with identical content. Preserve the original subject identities, faces, poses, clothing, object count, composition, viewpoint, colors, lighting, and all readable text and markings. Render the hair, skin, fabric, and other material details already present in the image clearly, with natural edges and realistic texture; correct blur and compression artifacts revealed by enlargement without adding or redesigning any visual content.
